situation:
You are the human resources manager at ARDENFIELD CLINICAL LABORATORY, a diagnostic testing lab that a single family has run for three generations. The owner (judge) has asked you to meet about the employee handbook that is due to take effect at the start of next month.

ARDENFIELD processes blood and tissue samples for clinics across two counties. Its overnight shift is the whole business: samples collected during the day are read between midnight and morning so a physician has results at the first appointment. The lab's certified technologists are hard to replace, and the ones on nights have been asking for two years for a rule limiting how many overnight shifts run back to back.

The updated handbook grants it. It caps consecutive overnight shifts and makes extra shifts voluntary rather than assigned, and the night technologists have already been told the draft says so. Read against the current roster, the cap lowers what the lab can read overnight by about a fifth. The lab cannot post the results everyone is expecting the following morning, and clinics are already calling to ask whether their turnaround is changing.

Holding the promised turnaround for every account would mean writing an exemption for the overnight shift into the handbook, and the technologists who asked for the rule, and were told it was coming, would watch it be withdrawn. Adopting the cap as drafted would mean telling one set of clinics that overnight service is ending, and the group practice that sends the largest volume is the one most likely to leave.

The owner (judge) wants your recommendation on what the handbook should say, which accounts ARDENFIELD keeps on overnight turnaround, what the lab should hire for, and how the clinics that call should be answered. You will present to the owner (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of ARDENFIELD CLINICAL LABORATORY. Business background is the same as the situation above. Your family has run the lab for three generations, the night technologists have been asking for a limit on consecutive overnight shifts, and the handbook that grants it takes effect at the start of next month.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend what the handbook should say, which accounts stay on overnight turnaround, what the lab should hire for, and how to answer the clinics that are already calling.
